parameters.content:
## Turn vague work requests into scoped briefs with adaptive n8n Forms and Gemini

### The problem
Intake forms are either so long that nobody finishes them, or so short that you spend a week emailing back and forth to find out what was actually meant. Both cost more than the work.

### How it works
This is a form that writes its own second page. Someone submits five loose fields describing what they want. Gemini reads it and decides three things: whether it can be scoped at all, how big it is, and precisely which facts are still missing.

If the request is really a support ticket or is too vague to rescue, it stops there and tells the person what to send instead - nothing is filed.

If it is already clear, the follow-up page is skipped entirely. Nobody is made to answer twelve questions about a two-hour job.

Otherwise, a Code node converts the gaps Gemini found into live n8n form fields - the right input type for each question, real dropdown options, four questions for a standard request and up to eight for a complex one - and the next page is built from that JSON at runtime. Every respondent sees a different form, written for their request.

Gemini then drafts a scoping brief: objective, in scope, out of scope, the assumptions it had to make, risks, dependencies, an effort band and what is still unresolved. The requester sees that draft on the next page and can correct it. This is the part that matters - the assumptions are shown back to the person who actually knows, before anyone builds anything.

If they correct it, the brief is rewritten with their answer treated as authoritative on intent, and the effort band moves up rather than quietly absorbing the extra work. The finished brief is rendered as a styled page in their browser.

### Setup
1. Connect a Google Gemini (PaLM) API credential. That is the only credential needed.
2. Open Receive the Request and copy the production form URL.
3. Edit the first page fields to match how your team actually describes work.
4. Optional: add a node after Render the Finished Brief to file the brief in your tracker, docs or chat tool.

### Customization tips
Change the question caps in Turn the Gaps Into Form Fields, swap the effort bands for your own sizing scale, or add a third form page for approvals when the effort band comes back Large.

## 1. Take the request as it comes
Five loose fields, no interrogation. Gemini then judges whether it can be scoped, how big it is, and which facts are genuinely missing - never asking for anything already answered or reasonably inferable.

## 2. Build the second page at runtime
Unscopeable requests stop here with an explanation and nothing is filed. Clear ones skip the questions altogether. Everything else gets a form page whose fields were written by Gemini for this request - correct input types, real dropdown options, capped at four questions or eight for complex work.

## 3. Draft it, then show your working
A Basic LLM Chain writes the brief - objective, in and out of scope, assumptions, risks, dependencies, effort band, open questions. The requester sees the draft and, crucially, the assumptions that were made on their behalf, and says whether it is right.

## 4. Correct and hand it back
Approved briefs pass straight through. Corrections are applied with the requester treated as the authority on intent - contradicted assumptions are removed rather than softened, and if the change makes the job bigger the effort band moves up instead of absorbing it. The result renders as a finished page in the browser.
